demand_scaffolding.w: Substitute $(p - q) = 9$ and evaluate $9^3 = 729$ to isolate $p^3 - q^3 - 27pq$

questions.difficulty_rationale: Requires recognizing the binomial cube identity $(p - q)^3$ and substituting the linear relation into the expanded terms.
questions.common_wrong_route: Attempting to substitute $p = q + 9$ directly into $p^3 - q^3$ and expanding by brute force, which leads to heavy algebra and sign errors.
questions.svg_caption: Identity Structure: Direct binomial cube expansion $(p - q)^3$.

hint_ladder.label: Identity Identification
hint_ladder.prompt: Which standard algebraic identity relates $(p - q)$, $(p^3 - q^3)$, and the product $pq$?
hint_ladder.hint: Recall the binomial expansion: $(p - q)^3 = p^3 - q^3 - 3pq(p - q)$.

hint_ladder.label: Substitution
hint_ladder.prompt: What do you obtain when you substitute the known value $p - q = 9$ into this identity?
hint_ladder.hint: Replace $(p - q)$ with $9$ on both the left-hand side and inside the $-3pq(p - q)$ term: $9^3 = p^3 - q^3 - 3pq(9)$.

hint_ladder.label: Algebraic Isolation
hint_ladder.prompt: Calculate $9^3$ and rearrange the equation to match the target expression.
hint_ladder.hint: $9^3 = 729$. Therefore, $729 = p^3 - q^3 - 27pq$, which establishes the required proof.

solution_moves.action: State the standard algebraic identity for the cube of a binomial difference.
solution_moves.uses: Binomial Identity $(a - b)^3 = a^3 - b^3 - 3ab(a - b)$
solution_moves.why_valid: Holds identically for all real values of $p$ and $q$.

solution_moves.action: Substitute the given condition $p - q = 9$ into both sides of the identity.
solution_moves.why_valid: Direct equality substitution into the algebraic identity.

solution_moves.action: Evaluate the arithmetic cube $9^3 = 729$ and multiply the middle product term.

questions.independent_check: Test with numerical values: let $p = 10, q = 1$ (so $p - q = 9$). Then $p^3 - q^3 - 27pq = 1000 - 1 - 27(10) = 999 - 270 = 729$. Identity is verified.
